interface.title: FCS-Protein Oligomerization Simulator
interface.stage_of_work: Experiment planning and interpretation: simulating expected FCS titration curves before or alongside measurements, and making figure-ready curves
interface.what_it_is_for: Simulate how the normalized apparent FCS diffusion time and the fractions of each species change with total protein concentration for dimer–monomer, trimer–monomer, or tetramer–dimer–monomer equilibria, then export the curves as CSV.

data.note: There is no data to upload or load. Every curve is calculated from the sidebar parameters: the model, Kd (Kd^E, or Kd1/Kd2), the labeling efficiency f, the labeled concentration C̃L and the concentration range Min/Max. Three CSVs were downloaded: fcs_dimer_simulation.csv, fcs_trimer_simulation.csv and fcs_tetramer_simulation.csv. Each has columns for total protein concentration, normalized tau_app, a blank spacer, then one column per species under a 'Fractional Concentrations' header row.

tree.general: Predict how a self-associating molecule's measured diffusion signal and species make-up change across a concentration titration
tree.specific: Simulate tau_app/tau_oligomer and fractional monomer/dimer/trimer/tetramer concentrations vs total protein concentration for an FCS titration, then export them

features.name: Model selector that rebuilds the parameter form
features.general: Choose a reaction scheme from a list; the input form then shows that scheme's equations, constants and concentration units
features.specific: The EQUILIBRIUM MODEL dropdown swaps the rendered reaction (D ⇌ 2M, T3 ⇌ 3M, T4 ⇌ 2D and D ⇌ 2M), the Kd definition equations, the constant inputs (Kd / Kd^E / Kd1 + Kd2) and the 'as dimers/trimers/tetramers' unit labels for C̃L and the range
steps: hover the ? help to read what each model means
read the updated equations and fill in the constants that appear for it
serves_tasks: Choose which association scheme to simulate

features.name: Batch parameter edit with an explicit Run and range check
features.general: Edit several numeric inputs (stepper or typed) without recalculating, then compute everything at once with a run button that first checks the inputs; switching the reaction scheme is the exception and recalculates at once
features.specific: Changing Kd/f/C̃L/Min/Max leaves the plots as they were until ▶ Run Simulation is pressed. Switching the EQUILIBRIUM MODEL recalculates the plots right away (simulationforproteinequilibria.py:803-805; the checker saw tetramer curves before pressing Run). Min ≥ Max gives an error instead of plots.
steps: type or step values in the number inputs (f in steps of 0.05, Kd2 in steps of 10)
note the plots have not changed yet (a model switch, by contrast, redraws them at once)
if the range is invalid, read the error and fix Min/Max
serves_tasks: Enter the binding constants and labeling conditions
Match the simulated concentration range to the planned titration

features.name: Linked observable + species-fraction plot pair
features.general: Two stacked plots on the same log x-axis: the measured signal predicted by the model above, and the fraction of each species behind it below, so you can see which species change explains the signal
features.specific: Top: tau_app/tau_n vs total protein concentration, with a second top axis for C0 (total monomer). Bottom: fractional concentration α for Monomer/Dimer/Trimer/Tetramer with a legend. The pair can be opened full screen with the framework's Fullscreen button (a viewing convenience, not a scientific step).
steps: read where the tau_app curve rises
match it to the crossover of the species fractions below
change a constant and run again to see both plots shift
optionally press Fullscreen on the figure to inspect it enlarged, then press Escape
serves_tasks: See how labeling conditions shift the measured curve

features.specific: Download CSV saves fcs_dimer/trimer/tetramer_simulation.csv with Total Protein Concentration, Normalized tau_app and one column per species under a 'Fractional Concentrations' header
steps: run the simulation for a model
open the file in other software for figures
